evidence.claim: The Chefs' Warehouse describes itself as a premier distributor of specialty food products focused on chefs and menu-driven independent restaurants, fine dining establishments, hotels, caterers, cruise lines, casinos and specialty food stores.

evidence.claim: CHEF's 2025 annual report states it serves chefs who own or operate leading menu-driven independent restaurants and other core foodservice customers, and cites growth from specialty products, center-of-the-plate products, acquisitions and distribution-center expansion.

HF Foods' 2025 Form 10-K states that the company markets and distributes fresh produce, frozen and dry food, and non-food products to Asian restaurants and other foodservice customers throughout the United States.

HF Foods' 2025 Form 10-K says it believes it is differentiated from large mainstream foodservice distributors by cultural and language understanding of the Asian restaurant community, specialized sourcing and a tailored product portfolio.

Performance Food Group's 2025 10-K states its Foodservice segment markets and distributes food and food-related products to independent restaurants, chain restaurants and other food-away-from-home locations; it also states independent customers typically use more value-added services and generate higher gross profit per case.
Performance Food Group reported fiscal 2025 total independent foodservice case volume growth of 16.9% and organic independent foodservice case growth of 4.6%.
evidence.source_title: Performance Food Group Reports Fourth-Quarter and Full-Year Fiscal 2025 Results

evidence.claim: US Foods' annual-report materials describe the company as a broadline distributor serving independent restaurants, regional and national chains, healthcare and hospitality customers.

evidence.claim: If foodservice distribution consolidation continues, independent restaurants may lose procurement fallback options, shifting bargaining power toward distributors, GPOs, cash-and-carry platforms and specialty suppliers with scarce sourcing or route-density advantages.

memory_update.text: CHEF should remain in the discovery lane for foodservice_distribution_dependency because it is a public specialty distributor with direct independent-restaurant and hospitality procurement exposure.

HFFG is a speculative micro-cap exception: very strong node fit through Asian restaurant distribution, but must be filtered hard for liquidity, internal controls, related-party transactions and execution risk.

Independent-restaurant supply exposure can be tracked through distributor disclosures such as independent case growth, independent sales mix, gross profit per case, proprietary/private-label penetration, procurement efficiencies and route-density economics.

Most true restaurant procurement software and GPO assets surfaced in this pass appear private, including Buyers Edge Platform, ArrowStream, InsideTrack, BlueCart and Meal Ticket; public-market exposure is more available through distributors than pure procurement SaaS.

node: Foodservice distribution, procurement concentration and independent-restaurant supply
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the foodservice-distribution dependency node found one obvious reference distributor and three discovery-lane candidates. The strongest underfollowed fit is The Chefs' Warehouse because it is a public specialty distributor directly tied to independent, menu-driven restaurants and hospitality accounts. HF Foods is a more speculative micro-cap exception with unusually direct exposure to Asian independent restaurant supply, but it carries governance, liquidity and execution risks. Performance Food Group is not obscure, but remains useful as a large-cap reference for how independent-restaurant case growth, private-label/proprietary brands, procurement efficiency and distributor consolidation show up in public filings. US Foods is included only as a reference anchor for broadline distribution and independent-restaurant exposure. No candidate is a recommendation; this is a research universe expansion only.
